name: payments-service
title: Payments service
summary: A client pays through a gateway; the payments API authorises with the card provider and queues settlement for a worker that writes the ledger.
whenToUse: Start here for any service that takes payments: every team draws the gateway, the authorisation call and the ledger the same way. Start from the queue and worker pattern instead when there is no payment.

slots.meaning: The diagram title, which is also its accessible name.

slots.default: A client pays through a gateway. The payments API authorises the card with the provider and queues the settlement, and a worker writes it to the ledger.
slots.meaning: One or two sentences that say what the diagram shows, used as its alt text.
The app or page where people pay.
What checks sign-in before a payment reaches the service.
The team's service, the group around its API and worker.
The service that takes a payment.
The worker that settles queued payments.
The queue between the API and the worker.
The payment provider that authorises cards.

notes.keep: Keep the gateway in front of the API, the authorisation call to the provider, and the queue between the API and the worker: reviewers look for all three.
notes.rename: Rename the parts through the slots. Pick the aws flavour for AWS icons.
notes.split: Draw refunds and chargebacks in a second diagram.
